answer: Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted identity anchored to a scarce external resource: each agent must burn a proof-of-work token bound to a unique hardware root, and peers verify it against a shared registry. A sybil attacker must acquire and burn one token per fake identity, so forging N identities costs N times the token price plus registry fees, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
